items.title: CFTC sues Utah to block its enforcement action against Kalshi and other federally regulated prediction markets, VitalLaw reports
items.content_text: - **CFTC sues Utah to block its enforcement action against Kalshi and other federally regulated prediction markets, VitalLaw reports** — The CFTC filed suit on October 26, 2026 in the District of Utah, following Utah's October 20 state enforcement action against Kalshi and Susquehanna. The agency argues the event contracts are swaps under the Commodity Exchange Act, that state enforcement is preempted, and it seeks declaratory relief and injunctions, making Utah roughly the tenth state the CFTC has sued over prediction market enforcement. (VitalLaw)

items.title: Prediction market litigation is split across three appeals courts, with the Third Circuit backing Kalshi against New Jersey while the Ninth and Sixth Circuits side with the states, Foley and Lardner reports
items.content_text: - **Prediction market litigation is split across three appeals courts, with the Third Circuit backing Kalshi against New Jersey while the Ninth and Sixth Circuits side with the states, Foley and Lardner reports** — Foley and Lardner says federal appeals courts are divided on whether sports event contracts are swaps under the Commodity Exchange Act: the Third Circuit affirmed a preliminary injunction against New Jersey in KalshiEX v. Flaherty, while the Ninth Circuit reached the opposite conclusion and the Sixth Circuit joined it on September 25, 2026 in the consolidated Ohio and Tennessee appeals. Kalshi filed a petition for rehearing en banc in the Sixth Circuit on October 9, 2026, and the firm maintains a litigation tracker as the cases move toward a possible Supreme Court test. (Foley and Lardner)

items.content_text: - **Illinois appeals the federal injunction blocking its prediction market licensing and tax rules, sending the case to the Seventh Circuit, Casino Journal reports** — Illinois has appealed U.S. District Judge Martha Pacold's October 30 order, which bars the state from licensing, taxing or prosecuting sports event contracts offered on CFTC-regulated exchanges such as Kalshi. items.content_text: - **Spain's gambling regulator says prediction markets need a domestic gambling licence, with Polymarket and Kalshi still blocked and no new framework planned** — Spain's DGOJ said at MERGE Madrid on October 30 that prediction market products qualifying as gambling under Law 13/2011 require a Spanish licence, and it announced no dedicated licensing category.
